subject: Renewal + premium SLO add-on: retainer, latency guardrail, and capacity uplift
snippet: Proposal for renewal with premium latency SLOs, 20% capacity buffer, and retainer for expedited support; requested updated pricing and DocuSign for signature.
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@helixpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal + premium SLO add-on: retainer, latency guardrail, and capacity uplift

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the conversation last week — summarizing the renewal approach we discussed and an initial ask so you have something to share with finance/procurement: 

Proposal highlights (attached):
- 12-month renewal with an optional 6-month retainer for priority ops and an SLA addendum that introduces a 99th-percentile latency SLO of 250ms for standard endpoints and 150ms for a new low-latency route.
- 20% dedicated capacity buffer during peak windows (we’d reserve an additional GPU pool for bursts).
- Faster incident response (1-hour P1) and a named escalation channel included in the retainer.
- Pricing: see Helix_Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx attached; we’ve shown both a committed and pay-as-you-go uplift.

Attachments: [Attachment: Helix_SLA_Proposal_v3.pdf] [Attachment: Helix_Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx]

Can you confirm the acceptance criteria from procurement (DocuSign vs. signed PDF) and whether you need adjustments to the latency targets or capacity baseline? If this looks directionally right I’ll send a tracked SLA addendum for e-signature and loop in Legal/Finance to finalize.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0129
From: Elena Morales <elena@helixpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@helixpay.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + premium SLO add-on: retainer, latency guardrail, and capacity uplift

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A few items we need to confirm from our side before moving to signature:

1) Latency SLOs: The 99p targets are promising but we need clarification on measurement windows (30-day rolling vs. monthly calendar) and whether the low-latency route has usage caps before degraded routing kicks in.
2) Capacity buffer: we like the 20% buffer, but we'd prefer a bursting model that scales to +40% for no more than 6 hours/day during scheduled campaigns. Can you map how the dedicated pool would be billed for that behavior?
3) Retainer: procurement requires a line-item showing retainer services (named escalation + on-call) vs. credits — we need that spelled out for our SOW.

We can do DocuSign for the addendum. If you can provide the SLA addendum with explicit measurement definitions and a billing example for the 40% burst scenario I can push this through legal next week.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Cloud Ops
HelixPay Inc
elena@helixpay.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: HelixPay renewal ask — need pricing + ops input

Folks — looping you in to scope changes requested by HelixPay (see thread). Quick asks so we can respond this afternoon: 

- Legal/Contracts: Marissa, can you draft an SLA addendum that uses a 30-day rolling window for SLO measurement, defines the low-latency route capacity cap, and includes the escalation channel language?
- Finance/Pricing: Lauren, can you produce a billing example that shows committed baseline + 20% reserved pool, and a burst path to +40% for up to 6 hours/day (itemize cost delta)? Please include how burst usage would be metered vs. the reserved pool.
- Ops: we need a short runbook itemizing the dedicated pool architecture and a note on whether we must pre-provision extra GPUs or can leverage on-demand for the 40% bursts.

We’re targeting a signature by 2028-12-06 if Helix legal signs off. Laura(?) — if they want an earlier kickoff for onboarding, what’s the earliest we can schedule a half-day ops workshop?

Thanks — Ben

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixPay renewal ask — need pricing + ops input

Thanks Ben — drafting the billing scenarios now. High-level answers to feed Legal/Ops while I finish the worksheet: 

- Measurement window: we recommend a 30-day rolling window for SLOs (that matches our monitoring telemetry and avoids calendar-month boundary artifacts).
- Burst billing approach: baseline committed capacity is billed monthly as a reservation. Bursts beyond reserved capacity are billed at a higher per-token rate; for modeling I’ll include an example where the 20% reserved buffer is included in the commitment and an on-demand spike to +40% is billed at 2.5x rate (capped daily).
- Ops provisioning: Marissa — we can support the +40% bursts using a combination of pre-warmed on-demand instances and reserved slots; full pre-provisioning of GPUs for the 40% would be cost-prohibitive for them.

I’ll attach the pricing workbook in the next message (Helix_Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx) and a short pricing summary for Legal to include in the contract.

- Lauren
Pricing & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@helixpay.com>
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@helixpay.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-30T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Updated SLA addendum + DocuSign (HelixPay renewal)

Elena — attaching a redline of the SLA addendum and a pricing worksheet that implements the burst billing model Lauren suggested. Highlights of updates: 

- Measurement: 30-day rolling window for SLO evaluation; clear definitions for numerator/denominator and traffic inclusion rules.
- Low-latency route: 150ms 99p with a soft cap at 5M tokens/month; after the cap we automatically route excess to the standard route and flag as an SLA-eligible degradation event (credit language in section 4).
- Burst behavior: reserved baseline + 20% cushion included in the commitment; automated burst to +40% for up to 6 hours/day billed at 2.5x per-token for overflow. Example billing table in the attached workbook.
- Retainer: line-itemized as a monthly fee for priority on-call, named escalation, and two annual on-site/virtual workshops.

Attachments: [Attachment: SLA_Addendum_Helix.docx] [Attachment: Helix_Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx]

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/helixpay/sla-addendum

If this aligns with your ask I’ll route to Legal and send the DocuSign envelope. Also proposing onboarding kickoff week of 2028-12-11 — we can do a half-day architecture review + ops runbook session.

Cheers,
Ben
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@helixpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena@helixpay.com>
Date: 2028-11-30T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Updated SLA addendum + DocuSign (HelixPay renewal)

Ben — thanks for the speedy turnaround. The changes look good and the billing examples are helpful. Helix legal wants the DocuSign envelope and will review the addendum today. We prefer the onboarding week of 2028-12-11 — please pencil that in and we’ll finalize after signature.

Two small asks before we sign:
- Can you add a short clause that the burst cap is subject to at least 6 hours’ notice for unexpected sustained spikes (we don’t want automated infinite bursts without a heads-up)?
- For the retainer, can you clarify deliverable SLAs for the two workshops (agenda and deliverables per session)?

If you can fold those two bullets into the addendum we’ll proceed to sign.

Regards,
Daniel Kim
Procurement Manager
HelixPay Inc
daniel.kim@helixpay.com
